title: Board automation activation payload
description: Body of POST /task/api/boards/{boardId}/activate-automation. Defines the lane vocabulary a provider imposes on a board. hadoku-task interprets only the fields declared here and preserves any others verbatim — additionalProperties is true throughout, on purpose, so a provider can carry its own pipeline metadata without this repo learning about it.

schemaId.description: The provider's own label for this contract. Stored verbatim; never interpreted.

schemaVersion.description: The provider's own version. Bump it and re-POST to update a board's lane set in place.

label.description: Optional human-readable name for the contract, shown in the board settings UI.

dryRun.description: When true, changes nothing and returns a preview: per existing tag, how many tasks carry it and where it lands; which tasks fall through to the Inbox; any collisions. The preview returns a digest that the committing call must echo back.

digest.description: The digest returned by a prior dryRun. Required on a committing call, so an automated activation cannot silently reshape a board nobody previewed.

lanes.description: The board's lanes. Order within the array is irrelevant; `order` decides rendering.

tag.description: The literal tag written on the task. Unique within the board. Lowercase, digits and dashes — it has to survive being a space-separated tag token.

order.description: Fixed position within its track. Never frequency-ranked.

editableBy.description: The only permission. 'user' renders left and a human drags freely; a runner may also route tasks here on release. 'agent' renders right, is writable only while holding a claim token, and becomes draggable-out once no claim is live so work is never stranded.

description.description: Optional note shown in board settings. Never interpreted.

$comment: Validation performed server-side is structural only: lane tags unique within the board, editableBy in {user,agent}, order present. We never reject a lane for being named something we didn't expect, and we never reject unknown keys — see agent-boards-design.md §5.1.
